calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Oilers
calls.body: The Canucks’ penalty kill is near the bottom of the league, and the Oilers’ power play is the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Canucks tonight. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.
calls.call: The Oilers’ power play creates at least their usual 9.9 expected goals per 60.

calls.head: Active D against forward-led
calls.body: The Oilers’ defensemen shoot a lot, and the Canucks’ not so much. Edmonton is one of the league’s best for shots from defensemen, and Vancouver is one of the worst. Watch the Oilers’ defensemen jump into the play.
calls.call: The Oilers’ defensemen take a bigger share of the team’s shot attempts than the Canucks’.

surprises.head: Tristan Jarry got lit up
surprises.body: Jarry allowed 6 goals on 23 shots, worth 2.1 expected goals: 3.9 more than expected. Starting goalies have a night this rough about once every 125 starts. Most starters don’t get one a season.

surprises.head: Vancouver hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Vancouver’s hit score in the close stretches of the game was 41, against their usual 100 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 35 games.

story.head: The Canucks steal one in Edmonton
paras: Jamie Oleksiak made his Canucks debut, after five seasons with the Kraken, and picked up an assist. Ryan Shea made his Oilers debut, after three seasons with the Penguins, and picked up an assist. Paul Cotter got the scoring started for the Canucks shorthanded midway through the first, but Evan Bouchard tied it 1-1 for Edmonton late in the period. Marco Rossi put the Canucks up 2-1 early in the second. Bouchard struck again late in the period to tie it 2-2. There were six goals in the third period alone. Jonathan Lekkerimäki, Max Sasson and Elias Pettersson (#40) scored three goals in just over four minutes early in the period to put the Canucks up 5-2. Vasily Podkolzin cut Vancouver’s lead to 5-3 less than four minutes later, and Bouchard completed his hat trick 24 seconds later to pull the Oilers within one. Podkolzin struck again on the power play with 43 seconds left to tie it 5-5. Cotter won it with his second goal of the night just under two minutes into overtime.

The Oilers had the better of the play. Replay the chances a hundred times and the Oil win about seven in ten. Kevin Lankinen made 32 saves for the Canucks, and Tristan Jarry allowed six goals on 23 shots. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Filip Hronek, even with Bouchard’s hat trick in the game, by our Swing measure. The Canucks moved to 1-0-0, and the Oilers dropped to 0-0-1.

items.text: It was the first game of the season for both teams, and the Oilers lost their home opener.
Connor McDavid extended his point streak against Vancouver to seven games.
Leon Draisaitl extended his point streak against Vancouver to six games.
The Oilers’ Owen Michaels played his first NHL game.
